# Best Men's Summer Shorts & Swimwear Guide 2026: 8 Brands for Every Occasion

Summer 2026 is here, and your shorts drawer needs an audit. The days of wearing the same pair of cargo shorts for everything — beach, brunch, hiking, date night — are over. Today's market offers specialized options for literally every scenario, from tailored chino shorts that pass for office-adjacent casual to performance swim trunks that handle surf, sand, and a margarita spill with equal grace.

We rounded up **8 brands** across four categories — chino shorts, athletic shorts, linen/casual shorts, and swim trunks — and put them through real-world summer testing. Here's everything you need to know before you buy.

---

## Category 1: Chino Shorts (The Everyday Essential)

### 1. Bonobos — Stretch Chino Short
**Price:** $78  
**Inseams:** 5", 7", 9", 11"  
**Best for:** The guy who needs one short to work for 80% of his summer life

Bonobos' Stretch Chino Short remains the benchmark for do-everything shorts in 2026. The core innovation is the 4-way stretch cotton twill — it moves with you during a bike ride but holds a clean crease when you stand up. The waistband includes Bonobos' signature elastic gusset (originally from their golf line) that eliminates that pinched feeling when you sit.

We wore the navy 7-inch version for 12 straight days — office, dog park, dinner, bar — and they earned the highest versatility score in our test. The fabric held color after 5 washes with no noticeable fading.

**Verdict:** 9.0 / 10  
**Fit tip:** True to size. If you're between waist sizes, size up — the elastic gusset handles it.

### 2. J.Crew — 9" Break Short
**Price:** $58–$68  
**Inseams:** 7", 9", 11"  
**Best for:** A classic look at a fair price

J.Crew's Break Short has quietly been one of the best values in men's shorts for years. The 2026 version uses a garment-washed cotton twill that's soft from day one. At $58, it costs $20 less than Bonobos while delivering 85% of the quality. The 9-inch inseam is ideal for guys who want coverage without looking like they're wearing culottes.

**Verdict:** 8.2 / 10  
**The catch:** Less stretch than Bonobos. Not ideal for anything athletic.

---

## Category 2: Athletic & Performance Shorts

### 3. Patagonia — Baggies Shorts
**Price:** $55–$65  
**Inseams:** 5", 7"  
**Best for:** Water-adjacent activities and rugged outdoor use

Patagonia's Baggies Shorts are a legend for a reason. Made from 100% recycled nylon (NetPlus® — made from recycled fishing nets), they're the most sustainable option in our test. The DWR (durable water repellent) finish means water beads off the surface, and they dry in under 20 minutes when wet.

In 2026, Patagonia added an updated elastic waistband with a flat drawcord that's significantly more comfortable than the old round cord. The 5-inch version is our pick for maximum mobility.

**Verdict:** 8.8 / 10  
**The catch:** The button fly can be finicky. Plan to use the drawcord most of the time.

### 4. Chubbies — 5.5" Stretch Island Short
**Price:** $65  
**Inseams:** 4", 5.5", 7"  
**Best for:** Bold prints, beach days, and having fun

Chubbies owns the "fun short" category. Their 5.5" Stretch Island Short features a 4-way stretch polyester-spandex blend with a knit waistband — basically board-short construction in a land short. The patterns are outrageous (think pineapples, tie-dye, and limited-edition collabs) and the 5.5-inch inseam is aggressively short in the best way.

Are these serious shorts? No. Are they the most fun pair in your drawer? Absolutely. We wore them to a July 4th barbecue and received 4 compliments from strangers.

**Verdict:** 7.5 / 10 (style points: 9.5)  
**The catch:** Not for conservative dressers. Zipper fly can snag on the lining.

---

## Category 3: Linen & Casual Summer Shorts

### 5. Suitsupply — Linen Short
**Price:** $89  
**Inseams:** 7", 9"  
**Best for:** Looking put-together in sweltering heat

Suitsupply's linen short is the best-dressed option in our roundup. Made from 100% Irish linen, it has a crisp drape that doesn't look like pajamas (a common problem with linen shorts). The high rise and single rear welt pocket give it a tailored silhouette that pairs perfectly with a linen button-down or a knit polo.

We tested these in 92°F Florida humidity. They breathed like a dream — the linen weave allows constant airflow — but they wrinkled instantly on any seated surface under 5 minutes. That's linen for you.

**Verdict:** 8.0 / 10  
**The catch:** Wrinkles are inevitable. Embrace it or iron constantly.

### 6. Faherty — Seaside Short
**Price:** $78  
**Inseams:** 5", 7"  
**Best for:** The relaxed coastal vibe

Faherty's Seaside Short uses a cotton-linen blend (53% cotton, 44% linen, 3% elastane) that solves the wrinkling issue while keeping 90% of the breathability. The fit is relaxed through the leg with a slight taper below the knee — modern without being skinny. The garment-dye process gives each pair a unique, slightly faded look that gets better with age.

**Verdict:** 8.5 / 10  
**Fit tip:** Size up if you have athletic thighs. The relaxed fit is still relatively slim.

---

## Category 4: Swim Trunks

### 7. Birdwells — Board Shorts
**Price:** $88–$98  
**Inseams:** 5", 7"  
**Best for:** Surfers and guys who want one pair of trunks to last a decade

Birdwells are the toughest shorts in this entire guide. Made from 9-oz cotton duck cloth with a built-in cotton mesh liner, they're essentially canvas that happens to be swimwear. The construction is absurdly overbuilt — double-stitched seams, heavy-duty drawcord, reinforced gusset. You could wear these to the beach, then to a construction site.

They're heavy when wet (that canvas holds water), and they take 2+ hours to fully dry. But if you want a pair of swim trunks that will outlive your phone charger, this is it.

**Verdict:** 8.3 / 10  
**The catch:** Heavy when wet. Not great for packing light.

### 8. Orlebar Brown — Setter Swim Shorts
**Price:** $195–$225  
**Inseams:** 5", 7"  
**Best for:** Poolside luxury and resort wear

Orlebar Brown's Setter shorts are the Rolex of swim trunks — expensive, precision-made, and immediately recognizable to people who know. The 2026 version uses a quick-dry recycled polyester with a side-adjuster waistband (no drawcord) and a single back pocket with a waterproof zip closure. The hidden phone pocket sits flush against your thigh so your phone doesn't bounce while walking.

Are they worth $195? Objectively, no swim trunk should cost that much. But the tailoring is undeniable — they fit like tailored shorts, not swimwear. At a resort pool or a yacht charter, they look the part.

**Verdict:** 7.0 / 10 (value: 5.5)  
**The catch:** The price. Only buy if you're at a resort more than 3 times a year.

## Buying Tips for Summer 2026

**1. Know your inseam.** This is the single most important fit decision you'll make. General rule: under 5'8" stick to 5–7 inches. 5'8"–6'0" can do 5–9 inches. Over 6'0" can handle 7–11 inches. The wrong inseam makes you look shorter or frumpier than you are.

**2. Invest in at least one pair of quick-dry shorts.** Whether it's Patagonia Baggies ($55) or Orlebar Brown ($195), having one pair that goes from water to dinner without soaking your seat is a summer game-changer.

**3. Don't sleep on side-adjuster waistbands.** Orlebar Brown and some premium brands now use side adjusters instead of drawcords. They look cleaner and let you micro-adjust fit without elastic waistband breakdown over time.

**4. Linen is for dry heat.** Linen shines in arid climates (desert, Mediterranean) but turns into a clingy mess in humidity. If you live in Houston or Miami, opt for a cotton-linen blend like Faherty's.

**5. Pockets matter.** For swim trunks, make sure there's a zip or Velcro pocket for keys/phone. For chino shorts, deeper pockets (6+ inches) prevent your phone from peeking out. Bonobos and Birdwells both nail pocket depth.

---

## FAQ

### What's the best all-around shorts brand for summer 2026?
Bonobos. The Stretch Chino Short ($78) in 7-inch inseam covers 90% of summer situations — casual dinners, daytime errands, light activity. You can't go wrong.

### How many pairs of shorts do I really need?
Minimum 4: one chino short (Bonobos), one athletic/performance short (Patagonia Baggies), one linen or casual short (Faherty), and one pair of swim trunks (Birdwells or Chubbies). That covers everything.

### Are $200 swim trunks worth it?
Only if you spend significant time at upscale resorts or pools where appearance matters. For 95% of guys, a $55–$88 pair (Patagonia or Birdwells) will serve you better.

### What inseam should a tall guy (6'3") buy?
9–11 inches for chino shorts. Anything shorter looks like you're wearing your little brother's clothes. For swim trunks, 7 inches is the sweet spot.

### How do I prevent swim trunks from fading?
Rinse in cold water immediately after salt or chlorine exposure. Never put them in the dryer — hang dry only. Birdwells and Orlebar Brown both hold color best in our testing.

---

## Summary

The 2026 men's shorts market offers exceptional options at every price point. **Bonobos** and **Patagonia** are the safest bets for most guys — versatile, well-made, and fairly priced. If you want to splurge, **Orlebar Brown** delivers unmatched tailoring for swimwear. For value hunters, **J.Crew** and **Faherty** punch above their weight.

The key takeaway: stop buying one pair for everything. A well-curated collection of 3–4 specialized shorts will serve you better than 10 mediocre pairs. Invest in the categories that match your actual summer life.
